What to know about Duke vs. Siena The Siena men’s basketball team will face its toughest challenge of the season when it takes on No. 1 overall seed Duke in the first round of the NCAA tournament on Thursday. The 16th-seeded Saints will meet the Blue Devils at 2:50 p.m. at Bon Secours Wellness Arena in Greenville, South Carolina, marking Siena’s first NCAA tournament appearance in 16 years. Siena earned its spot by capturing its seventh Metro Atlantic Athletic Conference tournament championship with a 64-54 victory over regular season champion Merrimack on Tuesday in Atlantic City, New Jersey. The third-seeded Saints finished the season with a 23-11 record. This marks the program’s eighth NCAA tournament bid and first since 2010. The Saints were also awarded the 2020 MAAC tournament championship and automatic qualifier spot before the season was canceled due to COVID. Duke enters the matchup with a 32-2 record after securing the Atlantic Coast Conference’s automatic bid with a 74-70 win over Virginia. The five-time national champion holds the best NCAA tournament win percentage of all programs at .750. The schools have met once before, when Duke defeated Siena 92-74 on Nov. 13, 2015. Siena holds a 4-6 all-time record in NCAA tournament games, winning at least one game in four of its last six appearances. Against current ACC programs, the Saints are 10-26 all-time but won their most recent matchup by defeating Florida State 80-63 on Thanksgiving Day in 2022. The game will be televised nationally on CBS, with Ian Eagle, Bill Raftery, Grant Hill and Tracy Wolfson on the call. Local radio coverage will air on JAMZ 96.3 FM, with national radio coverage available on the NCAA Radio Network/Westwood One Sports. Can I bet on Duke vs. Siena? Yes, as long as you’re not in New York. New York doesn’t allow betters to place wagers on in-state teams, such as Siena. Duke is a 28.5-point favorite (-100,000) over Siena (+6500) on FanDuel.
